(Bnss), 2023 for placing on record orders dated 07.11.2015, 09.12.2015, 15.01.2016,
23.02.2016, 25.02.2016 and 28.03.2016 as Annexures A-1 to A-6.

For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed and Annexures A-1 to A-6 are
taken on record, subject to all just exceptions.
The application stands disposed of.

Main Case :
Through the present petition, filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita (Bnss), 2023, petitioners seek quashing of Fir No.110 dated
16.06.2015 (Annexure P-1), under Sections 406/420 Ipc, registered at Police Station
Kalayat, District Kaithal, qua the petitioners and all the subsequent proceedings
arising therefrom, along with order dated 28.03.2016 (Annexure P-4), passed by

sentences.text:
At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioners stated that he would be satisfied if
his prayer regarding quashing of impugned order dated 28.03.2016, vide which
petitioners were declared proclaimed persons, is considered.

Learned counsel
submitted that the petitioners in this case left India in February 2015 along with their
families and Fir was registered in the month of June 2015.

They were not aware
about any proceedings initiated against them by any Court of law.

Proper procedure
prescribed under Section 105 (1)(ii) Cr.P.C to effect the service of summons upon the
petitioners was not followed and the impugned order dated 28.03.2016 was passed in
a routine manner.

Learned counsel further contended that the petitioners intend to
return back to India, join the proceedings and surrender before the Court.

So, he
prayed that the petitioners be granted protection from arrest, so that they can
surrender before the learned Trial Court.
Heard.

From the perusal of the record, it transpired that it was well within the knowledge of learned Trial
Court that the petitioners had left India.

So, it was incumbent upon the Trial Court to follow the
procedure so prescribed under Section 105 (1)(ii) Cr.P.C.

However, the Court kept issuing
non-bailable warrants against the petitioners on the address, where they were not living and upon
non-execution of the warrants, presumed that they were deliberately not appearing and thus,
initiated the proclamation proceedings.

From the aforementioned facts, it is clear that proclamation against the petitioners was effected on
the address, where they were not residing and had already left for abroad.

In this situation, the
concerned Court was to locate their new address in order to serve them, instead of issuing
proclamation.

When the petitioners had already left the country, there was no logic of issuing
proclamation at their given address, where they were not residing.

Hence, it is clear that the learned
Trial Court did not adhere to the procedure so prescribed under Section 105(1)(ii) Cr.P.C.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it is held that the impugned order dated
28.03.2016 (Annexure P-4), vide which the petitioners had been declared proclaimed persons,
suffers from material illegalities and is accordingly set aside.

Considering the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners are ready
and willing to surrender before the learned Trial Court, it would be appropriate to grant one
opportunity to the petitioners to surrender before the learned Trial Court within a period of three
weeks. So, the arrest of petitioners is ordered to remain stayed only up to three weeks and it is

further directed that upon their surrender, the learned Trial Court shall proceed further, in
accordance with law.
